claims.quote: The GRIA3 gene is located in the X chromosome and encodes for one of the subunits (iGluR3) of the alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR), an excitatory synaptic transmission receptor present in most parts of the brain.
It has been observed in patients with different neurological and cognitive disorders, including epilepsy.
Three different de novo missense variants of GRIA3 have recently been reported in patients with Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy (DEE).
Genetic analysis revealed that the patient carried a de novo missense variant in GRIA3 (c.2359G>A; p.Glu787Lys).
The p.Glu787Lys variant had previously been reported in a male pediatric patient.
